channel.title: Rage Therapy - Call of Duty News
channel.description: Recent Call of Duty news from official and reputable gaming sources.

item.title: Modern Warfare 4 increased SBMM in DMZ despite multiplayer backlash: Report - Dexerto
item.description: Infinity Ward has reportedly tweaked Modern Warfare 4’s DMZ matchmaking to give player skill more weight when putting lobbies together. | Source: Dexerto

item.title: Call of Duty might have swapped guns and tanks for knights and swords if an Infinity Ward experiment had panned out
item.description: As much as Call of Duty is criticised for delivering the same thing every year, reports occasionally surface of attempts to take the series in bold new directions, even if none of these experiments have so far seen the light of day. And it turns out a medieval Call of Duty was also explored at one time. Read more | Source: Eurogamer

item.title: 20-year Call of Duty veteran with credits on every Black Ops game laid off as Xbox restructuring continues: "I am proud and privileged to have worked alongside so many talented people"
item.description: He was at Treyarch since 2006 | Source: GamesRadar+

item.title: EA hires another former Call of Duty boss to take the lead on all Battlefield Studios' projects
item.description: EA has made some notable leadership changes within its studios group, and in who oversees the Battlefield franchise. Byron Beede, previously Battlefield's general manager, has been promoted to group general manager. Read more | Source: Eurogamer

item.title: Treyarch lays off lead Call of Duty writer and Zombies veteran after "approximately 20 years" of service
item.description: Treyarch's former Senior lead writer, Craig Houston, has been laid off after approximately 20 years of service with the developer. In a post made to both his Twitter/X account and LinkedIn , the developer thanked fans for their support during his two decades with the company and confirmed he was impacted by recent reorganistation within the studio. Read more | Source: Eurogamer

item.title: Call of Duty Endowment marks Remembrance Day with veterans' Valor Pack push
item.description: The Call of Duty Endowment is marking Remembrance Day and its 17th anniversary by encouraging Modern Warfare 4 and Warzone players to pick up its Valor Pack, with all of Activision's net proceeds going towards helping veterans find jobs. Read more | Source: Eurogamer

item.title: Former Call of Duty producer says older games were “more fun” with less SBMM - Dexerto
item.description: Former Call of Duty producer Mark Rubin has criticized skill-based matchmaking, saying it makes casual matches feel repetitive. | Source: Dexerto
